title: Residue-field rank criteria for finite-projective maps
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $\varphi:P_1\to P_2$ be a homomorphism from a finite $R$-module $P_1$ to a finite projective $R$-module $P_2$ (finite projective means a direct summand of a finite free module). For a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ write $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ for its residue field. If $\varphi\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is injective, then there is $f\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $\varphi_f:(P_1)_f\to(P_2)_f$ is injective and $\operatorname{Coker}(\varphi)_f$ is finite projective over $R_f$. If $\varphi\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is an isomorphism, then there is $f\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $\varphi_f$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00O0, Algebra, Lemma cokernel-flat, parts (1) and (3)

proof.text: At the prime p put L = R_p and K = kappa(p). Tensor cancellation identifies the K-base change of phi_L with phi_K. The finite projective target is free over L by Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing. Apply IsLocalRing.split_injective_iff_lTensor_residueField_injective to obtain a local left inverse. This is the private helper split_atPrime.

For the injective clause, the target is finitely presented by Module.finitePresentation_of_projective. Apply Module.FinitePresentation.exists_lift_of_isLocalizedModule to the local retraction to obtain psi and s outside p with psi_L = s times the retraction. The identity psi_L phi_L = s id spreads after multiplying by t outside p, using Module.Finite.exists_smul_of_comp_eq_of_isLocalizedModule and finiteness of the source. Inverting s*t and scaling psi by s inverse gives an actual left inverse (private helper spread_split). The localized map is injective. Exact.split_tfae splits its quotient map, and Module.Projective.of_split makes the cokernel projective; finiteness is inherited from the finite target.

For the bijective clause, the residue map at the prime is surjective as well as injective. Right exactness of tensor products shows that the tensor product of the local cokernel with K is zero. IsLocalRing.subsingleton_tensorProduct (Nakayama) makes the finite local cokernel zero; hence phi_L is bijective. Module.FinitePresentation.exists_notMem_bijective spreads this isomorphism to an element f outside p. IsLocalizedModule.map_bijective_iff_localizedModuleMap_bijective and the tensor localization universal property identify the resulting localized map with phi.baseChange (Localization.Away f).
